stem:
The diagram shows Reyansh holding his hand beside a lit clay lamp without touching it. His hand feels warm.

How does heat reach his hand?

options.text: Radiation — heat reaches his hand from the lamp without needing contact.
Conduction — heat passes only through contacting solid parts.
Convection — lamp particles themselves move into his hand.
Conduction — any warmth felt near a lamp is conduction.

teacher.key_rationale: Heat reaches the hand beside the lamp without contact, so the transfer is radiation, not conduction through solids or convection of lamp particles into the hand.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source force diagram into clay lamp and hand.
